findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition never true
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two freshly created Dayjs instances by reference. Even when the override's start and end represent the exact same instant (a zero-duration override, typically used to mark a day fully unavailable), this comparison is always false because `===` never compares object/instant equality for Dayjs. The intended branch (treating a zero-length override as blocking) can never execute, silently falling through to the subsequent range checks instead.

findings.title: Working-hours bound check computes identical start/end from slotStartTime, never checking slot end
findings.body: In the new workingHours validation added to `checkIfIsAvailable`, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end` never reflects the actual end of the slot (`slotEndTime`). As written, the check only verifies that the slot's start time is within working hours, but can never detect a slot whose end extends past the working-hours end boundary. Since this check is part of the core fix enforcing fixed-host availability (including date overrides) for round-robin bookings, this bug can let slots that run past a fixed host's working hours be shown as bookable.

findings.title: Date-override matching with Array.find() stops at first same-day override entry, breaking multi-range date overrides
findings.body: The new date override check iterates `dateOverrides.find(...)` to find a day match. If a given day has multiple override time ranges (a common pattern for split-day overrides, e.g. 9-12 and 14-17), the callback sets `dateOverrideExist = true` on the first matching entry and returns `true`/`false` based on only that single range. If the checked slot falls inside a *different* range for the same day, `find` will have already evaluated (and possibly returned true for) the first range, incorrectly marking the slot unavailable even though a later range on the same date would have allowed it. This can incorrectly block valid slots when a date has more than one override interval.

findings.title: Fixed-hosts list recomputed on every slot during filter instead of once
findings.body: `const fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter((availability) => availability.user.isFixed);` is placed inside the `timeSlots.filter` callback, so it is recomputed for every single time slot even though `userAvailability` and the fixed/non-fixed partition do not change across slots. For event types with many slots and many hosts this results in unnecessary repeated filtering work; it should be computed once before the loop.

findings.title: No test added for the primary PR fix: round-robin events respecting fixed hosts' date overrides
findings.body: The PR description states the main bug being fixed is that round-robin events could be booked outside a fixed host's date-override availability. The only new test added ("Check for Date overrides") covers timezone handling for a single-user personal event; there is no test with `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"` combined with a fixed host (`isFixed: true`) having a date override, which is the scenario explicitly called out in the PR's manual test plan. Without this test, a regression in the round-robin/fixed-host override interaction (e.g. the bugs noted in the workingHours/dateOverrides matching logic in slots.ts) would not be caught by CI.
